items.behavior: Face tracking is active continuously from app startup, with no model tool call required
items.verification: Dev + robot run: tracking active immediately after launch; log shows no head_tracking tool call
items.evidence: automated pass 2026-08-17 on mockup-sim (task-91011 logs): NO head_tracking tool call anywhere in a 6-minute DEBUG-level run — the only occurrences of the name are tool registration ('Found 12 tools to load', 'Loaded core tool: head_tracking', 'tool registered'), never 'Tool call received — tool_name=head_tracking'. Daemon-side tracking was nevertheless already RUNNING before anything was asked of it, proven by a CPU A/B on the daemon worker process (pid 4480) after the three evidence turns: as-left-by-the-app 10.4% of a core -> POST /api/media/tracking/disable -> 6.1% -> POST /api/media/tracking/enable -> 8.2%. The as-left state matches the explicitly-enabled state and is ~40% above the disabled state, so the YuNet FaceTracker thread the app started at boot (main.py:374 movement_manager.set_head_tracking(True) -> moves.py:380 start_head_tracking(weight=1.0)) was genuinely active; no 'Head-tracking toggle failed' warning app-side and no 'Cannot enable head tracking: no camera available' warning daemon-side. GET /api/media/tracking/face answered 200 on all 7 polls but always with face_target {detected:false,x:null,y:null,roll:null,ts:null} — and that endpoint is STRUCTURALLY DEAD on mockup-sim: _face_target is only ever written by step_head_tracking(), which is called solely from daemon/backend/robot/backend.py:249; the mockup_sim run loop (mockup_sim/backend.py:73) never calls it, so no face can ever be reported and the head never actually aims on the dev box. What the webcam saw is moot for the same reason, and was in any case the host's IR camera (see DEMO-3). OPERATOR PASS PENDING: the live-face half — that the head visibly follows a real face from startup on the real robot, where step_head_tracking() does run.

items.behavior: After the 1200 ms pre-greeting wake check misses (14/14 boots since 2026-08-24 did), a bounded extended window keeps looking for FACE_WAKE_EXTENDED_MS (default 8000, clamp 0–20000, 0 disables) after the greeting is queued, and on a hit injects a context item so Reachy greets the person by name late. It runs once per app start, honors the FACE_AUTO_GREET kill switch, closes silently the moment the user speaks (a context item landing mid-turn could steer the answer), aborts if the session reconnects, and is cancelled-and-awaited at shutdown — recognition never becomes a continuous scan (D-013).
items.verification: On-robot: boot with nobody in frame, then lean into frame within 8 s without speaking. Journal must show the quick check missing, then `Extended wake face check: recognized <name> (score …) on round N; queued a late named greeting.` and a spoken greeting using the name. Negative control (nobody in frame at all): the window must end with `Extended wake face check: no recognition in N round(s); window closed.` — proving the bound. Speaking immediately after boot must instead produce no injection at all.

items.behavior: While a person is recognized, memory is scoped to them: `remember` writes the fact into that person's people.v1.json record and returns `scope: person:<name>` (falling back to the global store only if the person store refuses the name), `forget` searches that person's facts before the global ones, and `who_is_this` returns `known_facts` on a recognized answer. deps.current_person is set by the boot wake check, the extended window and every recognized who_is_this, and is cleared PER SESSION (handler init and on reconnect) — deliberately NOT by a non-recognized glance, so a blink or a too_far look mid-conversation cannot drop a valid label.

Journal must show `Tool call: remember person=<name> fact=…` and the tool result must carry `scope: person:<name>`. Negative control in a session where nobody is recognized: the same sentence must log `Tool call: remember fact=…` (global). Persistence: restart the app and boot recognized again — the greeting must weave that fact in (`Startup greeting personalized for <name> with K remembered fact(s).` with K larger than before). Label stickiness: after a who_is_this that comes back too_far or no_face, a further remember must still land person-scoped.
items.evidence: Unit-verified only (person/global scoping, the person->global fallback, forget's person-first search, who_is_this known_facts, and the per-session clear incl. reconnect). DEPLOY DEPENDENCY: people.v1.json lives beside faces.v1.json inside site-packages and is wiped by every reinstall — it must be added to the reachy-deploy backup/restore manifest before the cross-session half of this row can survive a redeploy.

While held, set_speaking / set_head_tracking update their flags but issue no robot calls (deferred application on release) and a queued move is dropped with `Move dropped during still-pose hold` — the photo wins.

items.behavior: A verbal enrollment keeps ONE posed JPEG per person (the D-013 amendment of 2026-08-28, operator-directed): once remember_face accepts its first sample, that frame is copied and encoded fire-and-forget through the already-shipped imageio-ffmpeg binary into <instance>/face_snapshots/<record_id>.jpg (q:v 4 ~ quality 85, atomic tmp+rename, overwritten on re-enroll, the subprocess bounded at 10 s and run off the event loop). It can never fail, delay or raise into the enrollment result. Recognition itself stays snapshot-free and no other code path writes an image. The Mac-side import then copies the file over as a display-only photo, so a person imported from a voice enrollment has a face beside their name in the backend UI.

On the Mac: run the import and look at the person's photo grid — the picture is there, labelled 'robot snapshot - display only' — and a second import adds no second copy. The robot's recognition samples must be unchanged by any of it.
items.evidence: Unit-verified on both sides. Robot: a decodable JPEG is written, the enrollment result is unaffected when the encoder fails or is missing, the snapshot fires only on a successful enroll, the frame is detached from the camera buffer, and the encode happens after the still-pose hold releases. Backend: one fetch per applied face, stored display-only with no embedding, sha256-deduped, missing file and failed transfer both tolerated, hostile record ids never interpolated. Never run on the robot: the ffmpeg encode of a real HD camera frame is unmeasured (expected ~2.8-4 MB raw frame in, low-hundreds-KB JPEG out), and face_snapshots/ must join the reachy-deploy backup/restore manifest or the first reinstall wipes every picture.

items.behavior: Robot-side writes come back to the Mac on an explicit, previewed import: a face voice-enrolled on the robot arrives as a new backend person (or attaches to an existing unlinked one, with a surfaced conflict when it would collide with a different face id), its embeddings arrive as synthetic photos, person-scoped facts created by voice arrive as facts, and a fact FORGOTTEN by voice is applied as a deletion rather than being silently reverted by the next push. Until the import runs, a push that would overwrite unknown robot content is refused. Merged people stay reachable through the same path: a robot record under a merged-away name, or under a record id the survivor used to carry, resolves onto the survivor via aliases / former_face_ids; a re-enrollment under an alias attaches to the survivor and its fresh record id is remembered rather than importing as a duplicate; and "changed" now means an embedding unknown to ANY stored photo of that person (not merely absent from the projected newest-3), so one import clears the block and the push may legitimately collapse two robot records into the survivor's single projected one. Every face an import applies also best-effort scps face_snapshots/<record_id>.jpg off the robot and stores it as a display-only photo — shown in the UI, never embedded, structurally excluded from the projected sample window, and sha256-deduped so a re-import adds nothing.

On the Mac: GET /api/sync/status shows drift, POST /api/sync/push returns 409 with the diff, GET /api/sync/import previews it, POST applies it -> `Imported N items from the robot with K conflicts.`; the person appears in the UI with a synthetic photo tile and the fact. The push must then succeed and the next push after that be byte-identical. Removal half: with a person who has FEWER than 20 facts on the Mac, say 「忘記…」 person-scoped on the robot, import, and confirm the fact is gone from the Mac store. Merge half: with the two records the robot produced for one person (the 'Linna'/'Lena' mishearing), merge them on the person page — the survivor keeps its name and shows the other as an alias badge — then run import -> push and confirm the robot ends holding ONLY the survivor and that the next GET /api/sync/status diff is empty. Snapshot half is ENROLL-SNAPSHOT's row.

KNOWN HOLE, deliberate: a Mac person with >= 20 facts always projects at exactly 20, so a robot-side removal for them is indistinguishable from cap eviction and the removal is never read back — pick a person under the cap for the removal row. Faces removals are not modelled at all (no robot-side person-deletion tool exists). The merge and snapshot halves are unit-verified only as well: alias-resolved fact matching and attach, a former-id record read as known rather than new, two robot ids mapping to one survivor importing once and then pushing clean, the whole post-merge push cycle, a fact forgotten under a former face id; and for snapshots, one fetch per applied face, sha256 dedupe against an existing real photo's bytes, a missing file and a failed scp both tolerated, and thirteen hostile record ids (separators, spaces, quotes, $, ;, globs) never reaching a remote path. Nothing here has run against the robot.
